title: Szemeredi Core Definitions
description: Shared definitions and basic lemmas for the Szemeredi regularity pipeline: edge density, epsilon-regular pairs, regular partitions, and partition energy. Imported by both SzemerediRegularity and SzemerediCounting.

meta.author: Szemeredi (1975), formalized in Lean 4

mathlibDependencies.description: Graph structure for vertex and edge operations
Cartesian product for edge counting between subsets
Cardinality of finite types for partition energy normalization

originalContributions: Edge density definition for SimpleGraph bipartite subgraphs
Epsilon-regular pair definition with quantified subset condition
Regular partition definition combining equitability and bounded irregularity

overview.historicalContext:
The definitions in this module form the foundation of the Szemeredi regularity pipeline. Edge density, epsilon-regularity, and partition energy were introduced in Szemeredi's 1975 proof of his theorem on arithmetic progressions, and later refined by Komlos and Simonovits (1996) into the standard toolkit for regularity-based arguments.

By extracting these shared definitions into a core module, both the regularity lemma and the counting/removal lemma files can import a single source of truth, preventing definition drift across the pipeline.
overview.problemStatement:
Define the fundamental concepts for graph regularity:

- **Edge density** $d(A,B) = |E(A,B)| / (|A| \cdot |B|)$ between vertex subsets
- **Epsilon-regular pair**: $(A,B)$ is $\varepsilon$-regular if all large sub-pairs have density within $\varepsilon$ of $d(A,B)$
- **Regular partition**: at most $\varepsilon \binom{k}{2}$ pairs are irregular
- **Partition energy**: $q(\mathcal{P}) = \sum_{i,j} \frac{|P_i||P_j|}{n^2} d(P_i,P_j)^2$

Prove that edge density lies in $[0,1]$ and partition energy is non-negative.
overview.proofStrategy:
The module provides definitions and three proved lemmas:

1. **edgeDensity_nonneg**: By positivity of the numerator and denominator.
2. **edgeDensity_le_one**: The number of edges between $A$ and $B$ is at most $|A| \cdot |B|$ (every pair in the product can contribute at most one edge).
3. **partitionEnergy_nonneg**: Each summand is a product of non-negative factors (cardinalities, squares).
keyInsights: Centralizing definitions prevents the regularity and counting modules from using incompatible variants of edge density or regularity
Edge density bounds (0 to 1) are fundamental sanity checks used throughout the regularity pipeline
Partition energy is the key potential function: bounded above by 1 and increasing with each refinement step

sections.title: Preamble and Imports
sections.summary: Module docstring listing all definitions and lemmas. Imports Mathlib, opens Classical, and declares finite vertex type variables.

sections.title: Edge Density Definition
sections.summary: Defines edgeDensity G A B as |{(a,b) in A x B : G.Adj a b}| / (|A| * |B|), handling the zero case.

sections.title: Epsilon-Regularity and Regular Partitions
sections.summary: Defines IsEpsilonRegular (all large sub-pairs have density within epsilon) and IsRegularPartition (equitable with bounded irregular pairs).

sections.title: Partition Energy
sections.summary: Defines the size-weighted partition energy q(P) following Komlos-Simonovits (1996).

sections.title: Basic Lemmas
sections.summary: Proves edgeDensity_nonneg, edgeDensity_le_one (via card_filter_le and card_product), and partitionEnergy_nonneg (via sum_nonneg).

conclusion.summary: This module provides the shared mathematical vocabulary for the Szemeredi regularity pipeline. All definitions are sorry-free and axiom-free, with basic properties proved.
conclusion.implications: By centralizing edge density, epsilon-regularity, regular partitions, and partition energy in a single module, the full Szemeredi pipeline (regularity, counting, removal, and the full theorem) can share definitions without drift.
openQuestions: Should the module also include the energy increment lemma statement?
Can these definitions be generalized to weighted graphs or hypergraphs?
